artifact_role: independent primary-source numeric transcript; no scientific computation

source.title: Low-energy electron scattering from atomic hydrogen. I. Ionization
source.cross_check: Every numeric cell and row uncertainty was read in the page image and matched against pdftotext -layout output.

observable.channel: electron-impact ionization of ground-state atomic hydrogen
observable.theta_meaning: detected electron scattering angle relative to the incident beam
observable.E1_meaning: detected outgoing/scattered electron residual kinetic energy; E1 = E0 - EL, with EL the spectrometer energy loss
observable.electron_count_vs_event_integral_convers: pending; the paper specifies detected-electron continuum counts and DDCS but gives no explicit full-domain 2sigma normalization identity
observable.mass_frame_note: physical H experiment with incident/detected laboratory energies and angles; no finite-nucleus theoretical coefficient or event recoil model is supplied

uncertainty_and_normalization.quoted_uncertainty_kind: one standard deviation, one percentage quoted per angle row
uncertainty_and_normalization.normalization_reference: CCC H(n=2) excitation differential cross section at the same incident energy and angle
uncertainty_and_normalization.continuum_fit: polynomial in energy loss of degree at most four
uncertainty_and_normalization.E1_2eV_footnote: At 2 eV, less certain analyzer transmission makes the overall quoted uncertainty about 5% larger than at the other energies; the source does not unambiguously specify an additive percentage-point versus multiplicative interpretation.
source_locations: printed page 022709-4, Eq. (1) and surrounding text
